question_text: If 1, 1, α are the roots of x³ − 6x² + 9x − 4 = 0, then find α.

recall_prompt: Say which root relation you would use to find α, and what it gives.
insider_note: Two roots are 1, so the product relation gives α in one line; the sum relation is the check.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Product of roots
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two of the roots are known, so the relation that gives the third with the least work is the product: S₃ = −a₃/a₀ = −(−4)/1 = 4.

recall.must_convey: That the product of the three roots is −a₃/a₀ = 4.
accept: the product of the roots is minus a three by a naught which is four
use the product of roots, minus the constant over the leading coefficient, four
roots product minus a three by a naught, ante four
product of the three roots is four
heard_as: minus a three by a naught

steps.why: With two roots equal to 1 the product 1 · 1 · α is just α, so the product relation gives the answer in one line. The sum would work too (1 + 1 + α = 6) and is the natural check.
common_mistakes: Writing S₃ = a₃/a₀ = −4 and losing the minus.
Using the sum and product both, when one relation is enough for 2 marks.

steps.label: Find α
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 1 · 1 · α = 4 gives α = 4. Check with the sum: 1 + 1 + 4 = 6 = −a₁/a₀.

accept: one times one times alpha is four so alpha is four
one into one into alpha four, kabatti alpha four
alpha comes out as four, and the sum check gives six

steps.why: The sum relation is the free check: 1 + 1 + 4 = 6 = −a₁/a₀. Two relations agreeing is how a two-line answer proves itself.
common_mistakes: Writing α = −4 from a wrong sign in S₃.
Not checking with the sum (1 + 1 + α = 6 also gives 4).
